correctness.rationale: In a one-dimensional graph, a strong pair is arrow v→w precisely when w is its unique earlier neighbor. With only two nonneighbors per graph vertex, no pair can first occur after order position four, and the two missing edges rule out three simultaneous pairs. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all vertex orders for n=4..7 reconstructed exactly eight edge types per u∈U: {a_u,e_u},{a_u,f_u},{a_u,p},{a_u,q},{a_u,b_u},{a_u,c_u},{b_u,d_u},{c_u,d_u}; arrows u→v for distinct U-members are isolated. The connected core has 6k+2 vertices and 8k edges (including 2k leaves), so β1=2k−1, with k(k−1) isolated vertices; all H2 and higher vanish. The square loops span Z[U] and independent differences of p–a_u–q paths span augmentation ideal I_U integrally. Swapping leaves 1 and 2 reverses both types of cycles, so H1=ε⊗(Z[U]⊕I_U), while isolated ordered pairs are fixed under that involution and permuted by S_U, giving Htilde0=Z[U^(2)]. Proof for all n uses the order-position bound, not finite exhaustive computation. At n=4 the core is a single circle and no isolates, agreeing with known base example.
residual_risks: Strong matching complexes are filtration-induced: the result does not concern ordinary acyclic matching complexes, pure strong subcomplexes or clique-filled simplicial graphs. Homotopy splitting is nonequivariant; group action is integral homology only.
